# B2: do published Vensim and Stella models give the same results in Dynamist?

*Generated by `run_b2.py` and `report_b2.py`. Each model file is imported with `dyn run` (format from the extension), run with its own time settings, and compared with the output exported by the original tool at every saved time and for every variable both have. "Exact" means equal to the reference's printed precision: within 1e-5 relative, plus 1e-6 of the variable's largest value (Vensim computes in single precision, so a stock that should be 0 can print as -2.5e-6).*

## 1. Test suites with the original tool's output

- **SDXorg/test-models** (MIT, commit 21aab02): single-feature tests and sample models with Vensim output (`output.tab`/`.csv`) and, for some, Stella output.
- **SDEverywhere test models** (MIT, Climate Interactive, commit 5adeb59): Vensim models, each with Vensim's own `.dat` output.

| suite | format | files | exact | close | differs | no-import | no-run | crash | no-common | no-reference |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| test-models samples | mdl | 10 | 4 | 0 | 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 4 |
| test-models samples | xmile | 5 | 4 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| test-models samples | stmx | 8 | 2 | 0 | 1 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 2 |
| test-models tests | mdl | 145 | 98 | 1 | 21 | 15 | 6 | 0 | 2 | 2 |
| test-models tests | xmile | 62 | 43 | 0 | 4 | 12 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| test-models tests | stmx | 45 | 28 | 0 | 0 | 17 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| SDEverywhere | mdl | 57 | 33 | 1 | 14 | 3 | 6 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| SDEverywhere | stmx | 11 | 7 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| **all** | | **343** | **219** | **2** | **43** | **51** | **18** | **0** | **2** | **8** |

**219 of 335 model files with a reference give the original tool's results exactly** (65%); 2 more are within 1e-3. 43 run but give different numbers; 69 do not import or run.

## 2. Widely cited models (Vensim's own sample library)

Every `.mdl` in the local Vensim PLE install (367 files) was imported and run. **294 run**, 69 fail to import, 0 crash. There is no reference output for these yet (Vensim keeps results in binary `.vdf` files), so this section says only whether they run.

| model | runs in Dynamist? | why not |
|---|---|---|
| World3-03 (Meadows et al., Limits to Growth: The 30-Year Update, 2004) | yes |  |
| World2 (Forrester, World Dynamics, 1971) | yes |  |
| Urban Dynamics (Forrester, 1969) | yes |  |
| Market (Vensim sample MARKET: products, receivables, sales reps; not Forrester's Market Growth) | yes |  |
| Corporate finance (Vensim sample) | yes |  |
| Project management (Vensim sample) | **no** | model redefines TIME STEP / FINAL TIME / INITIAL TIME |
| Epidemic (Vensim sample) | yes |  |
| Rabbits and foxes (Vensim sample) | yes |  |

### The classics against PySD

Vensim PLE cannot export its runs (they stay in binary `.vdf` files), so each classic model was also run in **PySD** (SDXorg's open-source Vensim engine, itself tested against Vensim) and compared variable by variable, step by step (`pysd_ref.py`). PySD needed light, non-numeric clean-up to read these files (`clean_copy` in `pysd_ref.py`). Agreement with PySD is strong evidence, not proof, of agreement with Vensim.

| model | verdict against PySD | variables differing | worst error (in tolerances) | first variable |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| World3-03 (Meadows et al. 2004) | differs | 147 of 256 | 7.47e+03 | Delayed Labor Utilization Fraction |
| World Dynamics / World2 (Forrester 1971) | exact | 0 of 81 | 1.96e-10 | deaths |
| Urban Dynamics (Forrester 1969) | exact | 0 of 251 | 3.31e-09 | underemp to labor net |
| Market (Vensim sample MARKET; not Forrester's Market Growth) | exact | 0 of 50 | 6.95e-11 | pot orders not buying |
| Epidemic (Vensim sample) | exact | 0 of 11 | 0 |  |
| Rabbits and foxes (Vensim sample) | exact | 0 of 17 | 4.8e-09 | fox deaths |

**World3-03** agrees at the initial time and then drifts by 0.004% to 0.17% (population 0.03%, industrial output up to 0.17% by 2100). The first divergence is at the first step, in the two SMOOTHs fed by ACTIVE INITIAL variables (`Perceived Food Ratio`, `Delayed Labor Utilization Fraction`): PySD leaves them at 1 for the first step although their inputs are 1.17 and 1.34, while Dynamist moves them by one Euler step on those inputs. Two minimal models with the same pattern give identical results in both engines, so the cause is not yet found. Which engine matches Vensim needs Vensim's own run of World3-03.


### Every Vensim sample model that runs, against PySD

All 292 sample models that Dynamist runs were also run in PySD (`pysd_all.py`). PySD could run **185** of them (it could not parse 107). **Dynamist matches PySD exactly on 175 of 185** (95%), on every variable at every saved time; 10 differ:

| model | variables differing | cause |
|---|---|---|
| FunctionExamples__GET_VDF_source_ss_ | 9 of 9 | reads data from a Vensim binary .vdf file, which Dynamist does not import (it stands in a placeholder and says so). |
| FunctionExamples__RANDOM_UNIFORM_NORMAL | 3 of 11 | random numbers: the two engines use different generators, so the draws differ (expected; not a modelling difference). |
| GUI_Objects__all_controls | 4 of 24 | random numbers (as above). |
| ModelGuide__9discret__batch1 | 6 of 10 | PULSE TRAIN at its end time: Dynamist gives the pulse at t = end, PySD does not. Vensim's own output for PULSE TRAIN (SDEverywhere's `pulsetrain.dat`) has the pulse at t = end, so **Dynamist is right here**. |
| OptSensi__ExtendedPayoff__normal-generate | 10 of 15 | random numbers (as above). |
| OptSensi__SimulatedAnnealing__rastrigin3 | 12 of 25 | random numbers (as above). |
| OptSensi__StochasticOpt__easyStochastic1 | 4 of 14 | random numbers (as above). |
| Sample__WRLD3-03__World3_03_Scenarios | 151 of 294 | World3-03: the open difference described above. |
| Sample__WRLD3-03__wrld3-03 | 147 of 256 | World3-03: the open difference described above. |
| VensimDemo__WRLD3-03__WRLD3-03 | 147 of 256 | World3-03: the open difference described above. |

Why PySD could not run the rest: IncompleteParseError 87, ParseError 9, NotImplementedError 7, ValueError 2, RecursionError 1, FileNotFoundError 1 (mostly Vensim syntax its parser does not take).


## 3. Why models fail: the fix list

Causes are read from the error each failing file gives (first error only, so a file may hide a second cause).

| cause | files (suites) | files (Vensim samples) |
|---|---|---|
| other Vensim function not supported (NPV, FORECAST, GAMMA LN, REINITIAL, SIMULTANEOUS, ...) | 13 | 32 |
| quoted names and literal strings | 14 | 4 |
| A FUNCTION OF (placeholder equations) not supported | 0 | 17 |
| subranges, subscript mapping or dimension handling | 14 | 1 |
| a name the reader did not create (macro, data or array element) | 7 | 3 |
| model redefines TIME STEP / FINAL TIME / INITIAL TIME | 2 | 6 |
| file read without error but empty (legacy Stella .stmx) | 6 | 0 |
| lookup defined or called in a form the reader does not take | 3 | 3 |
| DELAY N / SMOOTH N not supported | 3 | 0 |
| XMILE the reader rejects | 2 | 0 |
| simultaneous equations (Vensim resolves or reports) | 1 | 1 |
| array constants written as a table (1,2;3,4) | 1 | 0 |
| other: {"error":"single_dimension_tabbed_array[A]: Expected ')' but found number 2; sin | 1 | 0 |
| initial-value loop that Vensim resolves (e.g. through SMOOTH/DELAY initials) | 1 | 0 |
| other: {"error":"shipments[Boston]: ALLOCATE needs the requests and the supply: ALLOCAT | 1 | 0 |
| Vensim ':' syntax (:NA:, :AND:, units ranges, ...) | 0 | 1 |
| other: {"error":"initial population TABBED ARRAY[MEXICO,A]: Expected ')' but found numb | 0 | 1 |

## 4. Reproduce

```
cd benchmarks/b2
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/SDXorg/test-models external/test-models
git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse https://github.com/climateinteractive/SDEverywhere external/sdeverywhere && (cd external/sdeverywhere && git sparse-checkout set models)
cargo build --release -p dynamist-cli
python3 run_b2.py && python3 report_b2.py
```
